newsitem.title: UK: Union go-ahead for BA cabin crew strike.
newsitem.headline: Union go-ahead for BA cabin crew strike.

text.p: Britain's Transport and General Workers Union (T&G) confirmed on Tuesday it has given the go-ahead for a strike by British Airways plc cabin crew over a five-month-long pay row.

A T&G spokesman told Reuters: "A strike has been authorised. They will be a series of 72-hour strikes," starting from next Wednesday. Staff have to give BA seven days' notice before beginning strike action.

The decision to proceed with strike action by cabin crew was taken after union efforts to bring BA into talks had failed. It also marks the first major industrial action since the new Labour government was elected on May 1.

"BA is sticking to its position of only talking to ground staff (over a separate dispute)," said the T&G spokesman. He said this approach sealed the decision by T&G general secretary Bill Morris to give his backing to a cabin crew strike.
Three quarters of BA's cabin crew were balloted by the T&G last week over whether to take strike action: 73 percent of those balloted said 'yes'.

The decision to press ahead with a spate of 72 hour stoppages was taken after BA chief executive Robert Ayling reiterated on Monday his hard stand against cabin crew staff last night. Ayling said he would not enter talks until cabin crew renounced their militancy. But he was prepared to talk to ground staff who are threatening to strike over a decision to sell of BA's catering unit.
Cabin crew are striking over a pay restructuring package, which is part of BA's wider commitment to axe one billion pounds ($1.7 billion) in costs by the year 2000. ($ = 0.600 British Pounds)
